question: Arrests may occasionally be made without a warrant. Which of the following is not one of those circumstances?

options.A: An officer may arrest for a misdemeanor that is not a breach of peace and committed out of arresting party's presence.
options.B: An officer must have probable cause that a felony has occurred and that the arrested person committed it.
options.C: An officer may arrest for a misdemeanor committed in their presence without any evidence.
options.D: An officer may arrest a person if they are suspected of committing a misdemeanor that has not yet occurred.
options.E: An officer may arrest a person if they have committed a felony, regardless of the officer's presence during the crime.
options.F: An officer may arrest if he suspects a person will commit a felony in the future.
options.G: A misdemeanor has occurred, and an officer must believe that the person he has arrested committed it.
options.H: An officer may arrest for a misdemeanor that is a breach of peace and committed in arresting party's presence.
options.I: An officer may arrest a person based on a tip from an unverified source.
options.J: An officer may arrest for a felony committed in his presence.
